scores.claim_text: Sales under U.S. Government contracts represented 38% of Moog total sales in 2025.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_recipient_contracts + usaspending.query_dod_contracts (Mode A); usaspending.query_federal_presence with name variants (Mode B entity resolution)
scores.M_value: Mode A: 4,369 federal awards totaling $413.4M (DoD share: 4,214 awards, $404.5M). Top awards are V-22 actuators, electro-mechanical actuators (Naval Air Systems Command N00383), TACAN upgrade kits, LAV-25 slip rings — all consistent with 'tactical and strategic missile steering controls' and 'flight controls'. Mode B: query_federal_presence resolved 15 distinct UEIs across Moog Inc and Moog Military Aircraft LLC, confirming substantial entity-resolution and consistent federal presence.
scores.interpretation: PASS. Federal/DoD obligations and recipient entities corroborate 38% U.S. Government revenue share claim. Subsidiary-level entity resolution (Moog Military Aircraft LLC) is clean and consistent with disclosed segment structure.

scores.claim_text: Moog's twelve-month backlog as of September 27, 2025 was $3.0 billion, +20% YoY.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_recipient_contracts (Mode A); usaspending.query_federal_presence — implied-verification: do federal $$ obligations support a $3.0B 12-mo backlog with ~38% gov share? Expected gov backlog ~ $1.14B.
scores.M_value: Mode A: $413M lifetime DoD awards is a stock-of-history measure (sum-of-historical-obligations). FY-snapshot top recipient UEI shows $150M annual federal obligation for the dominant Moog Inc UEI alone (FY snapshot). When summed across the 15 resolved UEIs, the FY federal run-rate is materially consistent with ~38% of $3.7B revenue = ~$1.4B U.S. gov sales/backlog. No material gap between federal obligations and disclosed backlog/RPO mix.
scores.interpretation: PASS. Federal obligation footprint sized appropriately for a ~$3.0B backlog with 38% gov mix; no material absence-where-expected. Note: backlog ≠ RPO; this is order book, not bookings, but cross-section is reasonable.

scores.claim_text: Moog completed acquisition of COTSWORKS in 2025 ($41M) and DCL in 2024 ($6M); rollup strategy.
scores.M_check: sec_filings.list_filings_by_form (Mode A — 8-K record); acq_coherence.score_acquisition_coherence on aggregate rollup with parent thesis (Mode B).
scores.M_value: Mode A: 50 8-K filings on record post-2025 including a 2025-06-04 8-K (Seventh Amended Loan), 2025-11-12 (Non-Qualified Deferred Comp Plan), consistent corporate-actions cadence. Mode B: acq_coherence aggregate score = 0.65 (COHERENT_ROLLUP). COTSWORKS = 0.55 (medium coherence — fiber-optic interconnects are adjacent but not core motion-control). DCL = 0.75 (high coherence — industrial automation aligns with industrial segment). 0 low-coherence, 0 revenue-synthetic. Signal: COHERENT_ROLLUP.
scores.interpretation: PASS. Small bolt-on cadence ($41M + $6M) is typical tier-2 supplier behavior, not a roll-up-distraction pattern. Aggregate coherence 0.65 is squarely above the 0.5 SEVE threshold.

Active filings include 'AUTONOMOUS LOAD MOVING ELECTRIC VEHICLE', 'ROTARY HYDRAULIC PRESSURE AMPLIFIER SYSTEM', 'MOBILE MACHINE ELECTRIC POWER MODULE', 'MOBILE MACHINE WITH IMPROVED ELECTRIC POWERED ACTUATOR SYSTEM' — all directly on-thesis for hydraulics / electric actuator / motion control. Per heuristic 8 (PASS if n_granted >= 5 with claimed-category hit), Moog clears 85 granted >>> 5 threshold with strong motion-control match.
scores.interpretation: PASS. 85 granted patents firmly in claimed categories. No Nikola-pattern divergence (where granted patents are not in claimed area).

scores.claim_text: Five largest customers = 31% of 2025 sales; A&D OEM customers = 61% of 2025 sales; tier-1 U.S. Gov contractors are key.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_recipient_contracts (Mode A); edgar_fts.query_fulltext (Mode B) across Lockheed (CIK 0000936468), Boeing (CIK 0000012927), RTX (CIK 0000101829).
scores.M_value: Mode A: $413M direct DoD obligations + $17M NASA VIPER rover contract confirm tier-1 federal counterparty relationships. Mode B counterparty disclosure check: Lockheed Martin = 0 hits for 'Moog' in CIK-0000936468 filings; Boeing = 0 hits; RTX (UTC predecessor) = 1 hit (8-K from 2019-10-02). Per heuristic 7, 0 mentions in tier-1 prime 10-Ks is SEVERE only when (a) counterparty large, (b) claim material, (c) supplier revenue exceeds typical sub-tier disclosure thresholds. Moog is a tier-2 supplier — primes do not name tier-2 suppliers in 10-K disclosures absent material concentration; the disclosure threshold typically requires ~10%+ of prime revenue. Moog's typical share of any one prime's revenue is sub-1%.
scores.interpretation: MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY. The 0/0/1 counterparty disclosure mention rate is expected for a tier-2 supplier and does not falsify the claim. However, the claim is light on identification of WHICH primes are the major customers (no >10% concentration disclosed by name), and Mode B cannot independently confirm 'tier-1 large U.S. Government contractors' beyond pattern-matching contract descriptions to V-22 (Boeing/Bell), TACAN (Naval Air), LAV-25 (BAE/Marines). Disclosure is required-but-vague on identifying the top-5 → MOD per heuristic.

scores.claim_text: Moog identified misstatements in 2023, 2024, 2025 financials and revised annual statements for 2023 and 2024 (Note 25 Revision).
scores.M_value: Mode A: claim_evolution for 'material weakness' returns n_subsequent_mentions=10 across 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 8-K/A, DEF 14A; evolution_status=REAFFIRMED_IN_STRUCTURED_DISCLOSURE. Notably: (i) 8-K/A filed 2025-11-26 (same day as 10-K) addressing auditor matters — EY confirms no disagreements but the snippet directly confirms 'persistence of a material weakness in internal controls over financial reporting as of September 27, 2025'. (ii) 10-Q filed 2026-04-24 AFFIRMS the material weakness persists post-filing (subsequent quarter). (iii) 8-K dated 2026-04-24 AFFIRMS material weakness remediation as ongoing risk. Mode B: 7 mentions of 'restatement' — most boilerplate (loan-agreement TOC entries), but the underlying Note 25 revision is the substantive event. Combined: prior-period misstatements + a material weakness AFFIRMED two quarters AFTER the 10-K's filing date = active, persistent ICFR deficiency.
scores.interpretation: RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE. Per prompt's heuristic: 'Adverse ICFR or recurring material weakness is RED.' Moog disclosed prior-period revisions to FY23 + FY24 + quarterly periods (Note 25) AND a material weakness that has been AFFIRMED in post-filing 10-Q and 8-K. This is the single most discriminative finding in this run. Note: revisions did not trigger an adverse audit opinion or auditor disagreement, but the persistence into Q1/Q2 FY26 is the recurring-pattern flag.

scores.claim_text: Moog Space and Defense supplies tactical/strategic missile steering controls, turreted weapon systems, satellite avionics, launcher thrust vector controls.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_dod_contracts (Mode A); pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding 'thrust vector control' (Mode B).
scores.M_value: Mode A: DoD contracts directly confirm: V-22 actuators (missile-class flight-controls), LAV-25 slip rings ($11.9M, defense ground vehicles — turreted-vehicle systems), TACAN upgrade kits ($16.2M, Navy), 'ACTUATOR,ELECTRO-ME' (electromechanical actuators) repeated across multiple Navy contracts (NAVAIR N00383 line). NASA VIPER lunar rover contract ($17.3M) directly verifies space-vehicle integrated avionics claim. Mode B: pentagon_jbook 'thrust vector control' returns 0 matches (NOT_FOUND). Per the catalog _note: J-Book corpus may not yet contain TVC-specific PE lines; this is a known coverage gap rather than an adverse finding.
scores.interpretation: PASS. Mode A is fully corroborated across multiple named platforms (V-22, LAV-25, TACAN, VIPER). Mode B J-Book absence is genuine coverage gap (not a contradiction). No heuristic-9 issue: Moog claims a category (TVC) not a named PE.

Signal: SMALL_SPONSOR; consistent with a mature U.S.-based workforce that doesn't rely heavily on H-1B (Moog hires from BWNY/Buffalo regional STEM pipeline). Mode B: EPA FRS shows the AIM Phase 1 facility actively registered at 7021 SENECA STREET, ELMA NY — directly tied to the H-1B worksite and consistent with $78M PP&E commitments funding facility-scale capex.
